most_important_question_top3.answer: Consolidated from G04-score.json (most_important_question_answer), G04-gtm.json (most_important_question) and G04-tech.json (mvp, capital_map); the three agree on scope and milestone and differ only on the 90-day dollar figure (see contradictions_noted #2). BUILD FIRST: the assurance engine, not the screen - an ASPN 2023 / pntOS-C-conformant integrity service packaged as an air-gapped OCI container that consumes a synthetic strait-transit scenario generator (3-8 sources at 1-10 Hz: GNSS jamming onset, spoofing pull-off, INS drift, clock holdover, hardware fault) plus public real recordings (TEXBAT ds3/ds7 via GNSS-SDR; Jammertest 2025 HDF5 on Zenodo) and bench telemetry (two u-blox ZED-F9P boards, an MTi-3 IMU, a conducted gps-sdr-sim/bladeRF stimulus inside a shielded enclosure), and emits per-source health, composite confidence with attributed evidence, an explainable fault/jam/spoof classification, a fallback recommendation with rationale and a bit-identical replayable audit timeline, validated against DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 Respond/Recover behaviours; a thin ECDIS-style HMI only as a window onto the engine; a reference plug-in subset published to the Open-PNT/ISTO community. Budget: weeks 1-3 ~$16k (interviews, counsel memo, technical spike); <=$80k cumulative through day 90; $100-150k through month 4-5; paid advisory board of one PNT-integrity engineer and one former ETV/QM (fatal if absent within 6 months). SHOW IT TO, in order: (1) NP004 Phase I awardees as selections post (~Q1-Q2 2027) and the incumbent SBIR vendor BlueRISC (whose $750k GPNTS SA Tool Phase II ended 2026-05-25) as a component supplier; (2) the PMW/A 170 GPNTS office (NP004 TPOC via the NAVWAR Small Business Office) and NIWC Pacific GPNTS/Raytheon software-support engineers as the candidate for the next open-topic cycle, a D2P2 or a GPNTS ECP via CRADA; (3) the Open-PNT/ISTO ASPN community and Army C5ISR Center pntOS engineers as a reference plug-in; (4) one commercial operator with Red Sea/Baltic transits or one allied navy officer as an unclassified paid pilot; (5) JNC 2027 (2027-06-07 to 06-10, Covington KY) as the single venue where all of the above are in one room. DEMO PROVES, against the Navy's own NP004 metrics: detection latency under 1 s at 1-10 Hz; correct classification on held-out synthetic and public real recordings with a quantified false-alert rate (targets >=90% synthetic, >=80% public real, <5% false alerts); former watchstanders (n>=6, pre-registered protocol) reach the correct fallback faster with fewer errors than with fragmented displays; every recommendation is explainable and replayable; the same container consumes an ASPN/pntOS stream unchanged so Phase II can swap in GPNTS ICDs without rework. WHY THE CUSTOMER CARES: PMW 170 wrote the problem in its own words (NP004, 2026-08-05), has paid for PNT situational-awareness software at least twice (2024 Phase I; 2025 Phase II $750k) and re-solicited it more broadly in 2026 with multiple awards planned; OPNAVINST 9420.1C 5.a(11) has required degradation indication and interference reporting since 2019; the GPNTS software-support ceiling was exhausted early by emergent fleet needs; GPS denial is routine (12 DoD interference tests Aug-Sep 2026 per NAVCEN; MARAD Advisory 2026-008) and M-code remains late in all three segments (GAO-24-106841, 2024-09-09); every Phase I awardee will need validated assurance analytics it does not have. WHY AN INCUMBENT CANNOT TRIVIALLY CRUSH IT (honestly a speed-and-evidence defense, which is why the verdict is borderline): receiver primes (Collins, BAE, L3Harris, Safran) have no incentive to ship vendor-neutral assurance that commoditises their boxes; Raytheon as GPNTS prime is a systems house on a ceiling-exhausted support contract that has not fielded this layer in seven years; BlueRISC's effort is an AI/ML module tied to GPNTS rather than an open ASPN/pntOS engine with a scenario/replay library; NGC2/Overmatch integrators lack PNT-integrity depth; IS4S - the one competitor who could build it - is committed to Army NorthStar (up to $41M, April 2026) and AF design-agent work and may prefer to license a validated component. The founders lose if they build a dashboard; they hold only if validated algorithms, the scenario/replay library with real recordings from civil/allied pilots, operator-study evidence and open-standard conformance make them the reference implementation. MILESTONE THAT WOULD JUSTIFY $2-5M (all four within 18 months, or stop): a funded Navy Phase II, D2P2 or OT - or a paid subcontract on one - with GPNTS ICDs in hand and a scheduled fleet/ANTX/PNTAX demonstration; at least one paying unclassified civil or allied pilot with a renewal; a named PMW 170 transition owner and documented path (ECP, RAISE/OSA container or Phase III) into GPNTS or pntOS; a counsel-cleared U.S.-person-controlled cap table plus CMMC Level 2 self-assessment and CUI enclave. If at 18 months the only money is Phase I-scale and the government has taken the layer GOTS or bought it from the standard-setter, stop - the evidenced money is single-digit millions and a raise is justified only by a transition owner with a vehicle, not by prototypes. Labels: FACT/HIGH on the topic, instruction and standards; INFERENCE/MEDIUM on costs, timelines and competitor behaviour; HYPOTHESIS/LOW on repeat-purchase economics.

If the founders insist on this gap they should spend no more than $30-60k and 3-4 months building an open-source, Dockerised 'TAK DDIL bench': 8-10 containerised ATAK-CIV/TAK Server nodes (emulators plus 2-4 physical phones) behind Linux netem, optionally EMANE/CORE, profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps (the DARPA FLUID regime) with scripted 30-minute partitions and reconnect storms; a scorer reporting time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicates/conflicts after reconnect, link saturation and a reconcile-log audit (CV <5% across repeated runs; a zero-degradation control run must score perfect); a CoT/TAK Mission API and public-Lattice-schema contract-test CLI; and an ATAK plugin module that emits an RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage and SBOM as a signed OSCAL-style bundle - all on public code and synthetic data so the non-U.S.-person founder can build it (INFERENCE; counsel to confirm), building nothing for Lattice or Ditto until an interviewee asks. SHOW IT TO, in order: three or four small vendors facing the next Jailbreak-series or Ivy Sting date (MatrixSpace/Adyton/AeroVironment-class and the 50-80 smaller API Marketplace participants); one NGC2 team-member T&E engineer (Team Anduril or Team Lockheed Martin) and through them the team lead's T&E manager; a DEVCOM C5ISR Center tactical-network S&T lead via the NetModX 2027 persistent-experimentation call and an ATEC/CJSIL integration engineer via the advisor; a TAK Product Center engineer at TAK Offsite 2027 - and not the Army CTO or CPE C2IN leadership, who have no test-tooling requirement to hand over. DEMO PROVES that a reproducible, vendor-neutral score exposes before an event the failure classes today discovered live at Jailbreak and Ivy Sting (arrival order of priority objects, duplicate tracks after reconnect, saturation on reconnect, missing audit events), that the same scenario file yields the same verdict across vendors and repeated runs, that the bench runs end-to-end on one commodity machine in under 45 minutes per scenario, and that the RBAC/audit bundle is machine-checkable and of a shape an ISSM/AO-adjacent reviewer would accept; it also proves what it cannot do - reproduce PoR waveform behaviour or exercise captures without a lab sponsor, so realism plateaus at 'generic DDIL'. WHY THE CUSTOMER CARES: a small vendor cares because failing at the sprint costs a fielding window and engineer-weeks on site (~600 people at Fort Carson for one event); a team-lead T&E cell cares because comparable numbers help it triage dozens of members before an iteration; a government lab cares only if the bench saves instrumented lab time - but ATEC now embeds collection in each prototype and reports in 1-2 weeks and C5ISR Center runs its own DDIL infrastructure, so the government's marginal need is close to zero (FACT: army.mil/295218; army.mil/293742). WHY AN INCUMBENT CANNOT CRUSH IT - honest answer: they can, and need not bother; Anduril gives away Lattice Sandboxes, TAK Product Center ships takcl and defines what 'conformant' means, Ditto can publish its own benchmark, C5ISR Center and ATEC/CJSIL own the labs and acceptance authority; the startup's only differentiator, impartiality, has value only if a government body designates the report as accepted evidence, and no public signal shows one intends to; the hard-to-copy asset is the founders' earned relationships and the published comparable result set - a credibility and hiring/acquihire lever, not a moat (moat 1, incumbent vulnerability 1). MILESTONE THAT WOULD JUSTIFY $2-5M: only an external designation - a written statement from DEVCOM C5ISR Center, ATEC, the Army CTO/AO or TAK Product Center that the bench's report is accepted pre-event or acceptance evidence, backed by a funded instrument (a task order under ACC-APG, a Phase II-scale SBIR or D2P2 after the cap table is eligible, or a CSO/OTA prototype agreement) and at least one NGC2 team-lead subcontract to run it across members; measurable form: one signed government instrument of at least $500k plus one prime subcontract and 10+ paying vendors at $10k+ each within 12 months. No public evidence suggests this event is coming inside the founders' runway (the one solicited DDIL test-tooling dollar already went to an established SBIR firm), so the plan is designed to detect its absence cheaply and end with a reusable open-source asset and relationships rather than a company. Labels: FACT/HIGH on the events, labs and open components; INFERENCE/MEDIUM on prices and vendor willingness to pay; HYPOTHESIS on the designation event.

BUILD FIRST: an open-source TAK Server/OpenTAKServer extension plus ATAK-CIV plugin plus a thin web companion (for the ~80% iOS wildland user base, because iTAK accepts no plugins), later a native iOS companion, that stores three things as CRDT-merged Data Sync mission objects - ICS 204 assignments, ICS 214 activity/status entries (with 201/202/209 templates) and a resource/LOGSTAT-style ledger - with per-field merge semantics (LWW-with-history for text, list merge for assignments, explicit conflict surfacing for quantities and double assignments, never auto-merged), a single Rust core compiled to JNI/WASM/Swift bindings with one shared conformance suite, transported as compact mission deltas over Meshtastic/LoRa and FirstNet; entirely unclassified, EAR99-by-design (counsel memo), buildable by the non-U.S.-person founder, nothing military-specific in v1. Cost: ~$50k and ~90 days to a demonstrable prototype (server extension + Android plugin + web companion); ~$100k and 4 months for the three-platform partition-and-merge demo plus a field pilot; $250k cannot fund a SLED sales function. SHOW IT TO, in order: (1) the state wildland TAK program lead running a WFTAK-using or COTAK-type server; (2) a Type 2 IMT planning section chief and resource unit leader; (3) the TAK Product Center Data Sync engineer at CivTAK 2026 (2026-11-18/20, Washington DC) - asking on the record whether structured form objects are on the Data Sync roadmap (kill if yes within 12 months); (4) an SAA grants manager and an agency budget analyst; (5) a Guard battalion S3 on a drill weekend as an unfunded dual-use check - not Army program offices, DIU or primes, whose buyer has been ceded to Onebrief/Anduril/Systematic. It deliberately does NOT try to prove a merge model worth licensing - that thesis is dead. WHY THE CUSTOMER CARES: every operational period the planning section re-keys assignments and status from radio, paper and chat; every reconnect after a division worked disconnected forces a manual reconcile; the IC defends numbers he or she cannot trace; the product removes re-keying and makes provenance visible inside the TAK app the agency already runs - with the caveat that the pain is real but tolerated (severity 3/5) and TAK Public Safety's own charter says adoption is gated by training, not features, so the 90-day plan tests whether it is worth $5k-$20k a year to anyone. MILESTONE THAT WOULD JUSTIFY $2-5M: twenty or more paying agencies or one statewide enterprise contract (>=$150k ARR combined) within 12 months of CivTAK 2026, plus written evidence that TPC will not add form objects natively, plus a signed integration or acquisition LOI from an IMS vendor, Ditto or a TPC contractor. The plan's own evidence says this is unlikely (agency ACVs low five figures; 12-24 month buying cycles; the licensing buyer has no reason to pay for what it can take from open source); if missed, the correct next step is stewardship transfer plus acquihire outreach, not a raise; if somehow hit, $2-5M would fund a SLED sales lead, StateRAMP/security packaging and a second (NATO/allied civil-protection) schema pack - still a small-cap outcome. #5 G29 cost: the score file's narrower version caps the bench at $30-60k, while score criterion 6 (and the tech file) estimate the proof of concept at $40-90k (HYPOTHESIS) and a credible lab demo at $150-400k. Resolution: cap at $60k for the software-only bench; the higher range applies only if physical phones, an EMANE mode and a lab-calibrated scenario set are added, which should happen only after a sponsor signal.

#6 Allied thesis vs. registry outcomes: E06's verdict (HYPOTHESIS/MEDIUM) is that an EU/NATO-domiciled interoperability company is the larger and more open opportunity for this team, yet every coalition/NATO-facing gap in the registry (G01, G12, G24, G30) was killed, largely because NATO ACT/NCIA build or buy that layer themselves and the founders' primary interest is the U.S. market. Not resolved: recorded as an untested hypothesis and listed under do_not_do as something not to treat as validated. E06 also notes the German founder's U.S. permanent residency may pull executive management outside the EU for EDF/EDIP control tests - directly in tension with the U.S.-person-controlled cap table SBIR requires; needs counsel.

#7 SBIR reauthorization details: E07-F2 (HYPOTHESIS/LOW) says S. 3971 may have rewritten eligibility rules; this session's search found law-firm commentary (GM Law; Crowell & Moring) that the reauthorization 'expanded scrutiny around foreign ownership and influence' but no verified change to the 13 CFR 121.702 >50% test. The founder-fit analysis assumes the test is unchanged (INFERENCE/MEDIUM); counsel must confirm against the enacted text.

#8 Ranking vs. founder-fit score: G29 has the highest founder-fit composite (4.2) but ranks third because the ranking criterion is probability of a fundable milestone within 12 months; G04 (3.3) ranks first because it is the only opportunity with an evidenced program office that has already paid for this class of software. The two orderings are both reported so neither is hidden.

#9 E07 segment labels: E07's regulatory matrix uses assumed segment labels that do not match the master S01-S14 taxonomy (E07 flags this itself). No conclusion depends on the labels because the regulatory judgments attach to the described function.

#10 NP004 status: G04-verdicts (market skeptic) treats the NP004 closure on 2026-09-23 as 'no live buyer'; the gtm treats awardee subcontracting as the primary door. Both are consistent with today's facts: this session's search (2026-09-26) found no selections posted, so the awardee door is future-dated (~Q1-Q2 2027, INFERENCE) and is stated as such.
